claims.paraphrase: Page title.
createAuthChannel is the supported way to add a second audience's login.
Pointer to the add-a-second-audience walkthrough.
Section heading.
The built-in owner/editor magic-link model is the default; the channel serves a different audience.
The channel is not a menu of interchangeable auth strategies.
The site supplies delivery, lookup, identifier shape, and challenge; the factory owns the security disciplines.
normalize must be idempotent, canonical per identity, and injective across people.
A lossy normalize maps two people onto one identity's budget.
lookup's subject must be stable and canonical per person.
challenge must really verify a human; the factory cannot tell a real check from always true.
The challenge is the whole economic bound on guessing a code.
Getting an obligated input wrong voids the factory's other guarantees.
Section heading.
No identity-keyed control may deny, delay, or destroy; it escalates or only logs.
The rule came from three failed design rounds and has no exception.
Lead-in to the three consequences.
Escalation carries the wire result challenge-required rather than a hard failure.
An escalated action charges no attempt, consumes no code, and fails nothing.
A failed challenge on an escalated action returns challenge-required again.
Eviction keys on the requester's own bucket, so a caller crowds out only its own rows.
The anti-abuse spend ceiling only logs at error and never denies a member.
Section heading.
Every action asserts matching Origin and https before other logic, throwing a plain 403.
The check mirrors the admin guard's origin rule, applied to routes the guard never covers.
Section heading.
Identity is a salted hash with s: or c: prefixes over the subject or contact.
The prefixes prevent collisions and the per-deployment salt prevents reversal.
Logs correlate on the first 16 hex characters of the hash, never the contact.
Pointer to the log events reference.
Section heading.
Codes are drawn by rejection sampling over a Web Crypto random range, avoiding modulo bias.
Vale directive and comment marking a document identifier.
NIST SP 800-63B's guidance assumes secrets are drawn by a proper random generator.
Vale directive restoring the units rule.
Section heading.
A confirmed code mints a channel session resolved by the same hashed lookup as admin sessions.
Logging out destroys that one session row.
revokeSessions ends every session for an identity, a deliberate destructive capability for site code.
Section heading.
A console-printing dev transport makes a roster oracle, since delivery runs only for known subjects.
A capture transport carries the same risk and must never point at real contacts.
Such a transport lands plaintext one-time codes in Workers Logs when run deployed with observability.
Keep dev and capture transports strictly local, gated like cairn's dev backend.
Section heading.
A site still owns normalize, lookup, and challenge correctness and a real delivery mechanism.
A stale roster lookup is a data problem the factory cannot detect.
Pointers to the auth crypto reference and the second-audience page.
